facts.statement: The species Sonidosaurus saihangaobiensis was described by Xu and colleagues in 2006.
facts.quote: The type species, Sonidosaurus saihangaobiensis, was described by Xu, Zhang, Tan, Zhao, and Tan in 2006.

facts.statement: Sonidosaurus lived in what is now Inner Mongolia.
facts.quote: It was a titanosaur which lived in what is now Inner Mongolia.

facts.statement: Sonidosaurus was a small titanosaur approximately 9 meters (30 feet) long.
facts.quote: It was a small titanosaur, about 9 meters (30 ft) long.

facts.statement: The fossils were first discovered in 2001 in the Saihangaobi, Iren Dabasu Formation, a site that later yielded Gigantoraptor remains.
facts.quote: It was first discovered in the Saihangaobi, Iren Dabasu (Erlian) Formation, in 2001 in a quarry which would later yield the remains of Gigantoraptor.

facts.statement: A 2017 review classified Sonidosaurus as a lithostrotian titanosaur with possible saltasaurid affinities.
facts.quote: In a 2017 review of Asian titanosaurs, Sonidosaurus was considered a lithostrotian titanosaur, with possible saltasaurid affinities.

facts.statement: Sonidosaurus is the only known sauropod in the Iren Dabasu Fauna.
facts.quote: Sonidosaurus in the only known sauropod of the Iren Dabasu Fauna.

facts.statement: Sonidosaurus lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
